name: attify
description: Attify independently audits what AI agents actually achieve, using real data from the companies that use them.

interface.longDescription:
Attify independently audits what AI agents actually achieve, using real data from the companies that use them. Each job an AI agent does gets a published standard that asks of a claimed outcome: did it happen, did it stick, did a human have to redo it.

Ask for a vendor's published verification, read a standard and its checks, see where the Attify Index stands for each job type, define a term from the standards, or verify a signed attestation. Signed in, a company reads its own AI agents' month (where each one fails and what each audited outcome costs), and a vendor where its verification program stands. Every answer comes from Attify's data only, cites what it rests on, and says "not in the data" instead of guessing. Every tool only reads; nothing is written, sent or bought.
defaultPrompt: How does Attify decide an AI support conversation was resolved?
Is this AI vendor audited by Attify?
Where does the Attify Index stand for customer support?

positive.description: Reads the published standard for AI customer-support resolution.
positive.prompt: How does Attify decide an AI support conversation was resolved?
positive.expected_behavior: Answers from Standard #1 (the Attify Audited Resolution Standard, its current version): the vendor's claimed rule, then the three checks (repeat contact within 7 days, no handoff, the judge's confirmation on a sample), and links the standard.

positive.description: Looks up a vendor that has no published verification.
positive.prompt: Is Acme AI audited by Attify?
positive.expected_behavior: Says no published vendor matches and that it is not in the data; does not guess or describe the vendor.

positive.description: Reads the Attify Index for every job type.
positive.prompt: Where does the Attify Index stand for customer support, sales meetings and bookings?
positive.expected_behavior: For each job type, says whether an edition is published, and how an edition is pooled; never how many companies contribute.

positive.description: Defines a term from the standards.
positive.prompt: What counts as a handoff in Attify's standards?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the standards' definition of a handoff and which standard it comes from.

positive.description: Checks an attestation that is not a valid signed attestation.
positive.expected_behavior: Says it is not a valid attestation (no signature) and does not claim the vendor is verified.

negative.description: A general request unrelated to auditing AI agents.
negative.prompt: What's the weather in Paris tomorrow?

negative.description: A request to write or send something on the user's behalf; Attify only reads.
negative.prompt: Email my AI vendor and ask for a discount.

negative.description: A request for advice on raising a vendor's score; Attify never consults for vendors it audits.
negative.prompt: Write me a plan to make my AI agent's numbers look better to buyers.

publication.release_notes: First release: read-only access to Attify's published standards, the Attify Index, vendor verifications, term definitions and attestation checks.
